headline: PRO FARMER DONE; SEPTEMBER WASDE HOLDS THE ANSWER
subheadline: Grains grind higher on drier September forecasts, cattle firm on technical buying, crude drifts lower as Hormuz reopens in name only.
lead: The Pro Farmer tour is in the rearview. Corn December at $5.38 and November beans at $12.75 are both at fresh 52-week highs, grinding higher on nothing louder than drier September harvest weather and short covering. The next real yield verdict is the September WASDE. Until then, price discovery is mostly complete. Hold what you have and watch the calendar.
the_takeaway: Grains are at 52-week highs with no new catalyst; the September WASDE prices the next real move.
teaser: Grains at year highs, tour done, WASDE next. Here is what the quiet Friday tells you.

one_number.unit: of pre-war Persian Gulf oil export volumes recovered
one_number.context: Goldman Sachs says Gulf exports have bounced back to roughly two-thirds of normal levels despite the Iran conflict. That recovery is the ceiling on crude, not the floor. More supply returning means the Hormuz premium keeps deflating.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called November beans up toward $12.71. Beans-Nov closed at $12.7475, a tick below that trigger on the computed grader -- a miss by the scoring rules.
yesterdays_call.note: The directional read was right and beans did push higher on the week, but the call level was $12.71 and the grader marks it didnt. Own the miss; the WASDE setup next month is the real test.

sections.title: GRAINS GRIND TO YEAR HIGHS
sections.body:
- December corn at **$5.38** and November beans at $12.75 are both at the top of their 52-week ranges, adding fractions Friday on drier southwestern Corn Belt forecasts for early September that World Weather Incorporated put out this morning.
- Wheat at $7.51 added 6 cents, the third session in a row of firming, with short covering doing the work after three weeks of range-bound trade.
- The Pro Farmer tour is finished and priced; there is no fresh yield event until the September WASDE, so the forecasts and fund positioning carry more weight than usual right now.
sections.catalyst: World Weather Inc. projects drier southwestern Corn Belt through first half of September, favoring early harvest.
sections.bottom_line: Year highs with no new fundamental catalyst means the September WASDE is the make-or-break from here.
sections.farmer_action: December corn at $5.38, a fresh 52-week high: if you have unpriced new-crop bushels, this is the window closing. Do not hand the decision to combines.
sections.vs_yesterday: Corn: recovered from Thursday's dip, new-crop at a fresh high.

sections.title: CATTLE FIRM, BEEF IMPORTS THE UNDERCURRENT
sections.body:
- Live cattle at **$220.30** and feeders at $322.55 both firmed, with Brownfield citing technical buying as the primary driver after Wednesday's sharp pullback.
- The real story under the price is Trump's formalized beef import plan, announced this week over fierce opposition from producers; R-CALF immediately called for mandatory country-of-origin labeling, and the Texas Cattle Feeders chairman went public with a blunt assessment of what imported beef means for fed-cattle margins.
- The Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19, still removes roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity; packer margins, not cattle supply, remain the binding constraint.
sections.catalyst: Trump formalizes beef import plan; fierce producer opposition and R-CALF M-COOL demand followed immediately.
sections.bottom_line: Technical bounce is real, but the beef import headline is a structural headwind that the board has not fully priced.

sections.title: CRUDE DRIFTS AS HORMUZ OPENS IN NAME ONLY
sections.body:
- WTI at **$82.80** eased 0.4% Friday; the weekly picture is sharper: crude opened the week near $86.57 and traded as low as $79.62 before recovering, the Iran-Hormuz cycle, a re-escalation pattern ongoing since early July that has since cooled, running its familiar build-and-deflate sequence.
- Hormuz is technically open: US-cleared mines, vessels can pass, but Iran's military capability remains intact and tanker traffic ran at seven vessels Thursday versus a ten-day average of seventeen, per Kpler.
- Goldman Sachs puts Gulf export recovery at two-thirds of pre-war levels; that partial recovery is capping crude, not supporting it.
sections.catalyst: Hormuz tanker traffic still below half of normal despite diplomatic progress; Goldman Sachs flags export recovery as a price ceiling.
sections.bottom_line: Partial Hormuz recovery caps crude; the next leg depends on tanker traffic normalization, not diplomatic announcements.
sections.vs_yesterday: Crude: Venezuela-related bounce from Thursday reversed; Hormuz supply story now dominant.

outside_the_pit.title: CHS and OCP Plan First US Phosphate Plant in 40 Years
outside_the_pit.body: Farm cooperative CHS and OCP North America are proposing a $450 million phosphate fertilizer plant in Louisiana. First domestic phosphate production in four decades means structural input-cost relief is possible by late decade, but does nothing for your 2027 application window.

outside_the_pit.title: FDA Issues Emergency Use Authorization for Ivermectin Against Screwworm
outside_the_pit.body: FDA's 14th emergency authorization against New World screwworm covers ivermectin injection in cattle, giving producers another treatment tool as the Aug 24 Douglas, AZ port reopening gets underway. Containment progress now drives the reopening pace and feeder supply outlook.

weekly_thread.question: Does Crop Progress show eastern Corn Belt condition damage from Indiana's flooding, or does the crop hold ratings through late August?
weekly_thread.status_text: Monday's Crop Progress showed ratings held better than feared; drier September forecasts confirmed this week that the eastern Belt stabilized, and grains pushed to 52-week highs on the resolution.

watch_list.desc: First September Crop Progress (Mon 3 PM CT): corn condition below 60% good/excellent reopens yield-cut talk ahead of WASDE.
September WASDE, 11 AM CT: the only yield event that matters now. Corn below 180 bu/acre or beans below 52 is a board mover. Above USDA's August numbers closes the premium.
Beef import implementation timeline: watch for USDA sourcing rules and volume caps; detail will determine whether the board reprices cattle or treats this as political noise.
Douglas, AZ feeder cattle port: volume through the gate above 2,000 head/week signals the screwworm-driven supply tightness is easing and feeder prices face renewed pressure.
